M/S Sharma Old Body Parts And 19 Others vs Sri Rohit Singh
Sajwan, Ssp/ Police ... on 15 May, 2024

Author: Rohit Ranjan Agarwal
Bench: Rohit Ranjan Agarwal
High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad
?Neutral Citation No. - 2024:Ahc:89963
Court No. - 51
Case :- Contempt Application (Civil) No. - 3149 of 2023
Applicant :- M/S Sharma Old Body Parts And 19 Others
Opposite Party :- Sri Rohit Singh Sajwan, Ssp/ Police Commissioner & 2 Others
Counsel for Applicant :- Prem Narayan Rai,Ram Kumar Pandey,Raza Hasnain,Shahabuddin
Hon'ble Rohit Ranjan Agarwal,J.
1.

entities.text: High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Reply to the compliance affidavit, filed today, is taken on record.

2. The applicants, who are twenty in numbers, had approached the writ Court through Writ-C No.34843 of 2022 seeking a writ of mandamus commanding the opposite parties not to interfere in the opening of their shop/firm at business place Sotiganj Bazar, District Meerut, which was forcibly closed down by oral order.

3. The writ Court, on the instructions being placed by learned Standing Counsel, disposed of the writ petition giving liberty to the petitioners therein to raise their grievance individually before Commissioner of Police, Meerut who was to look into the matter and take appropriate action.

4. In the aforesaid writ petition, on 15.02.2023, following order was passed by the writ Court :-
"Heard Sri H.R. Mishra, learned senior advocate assisted by Sri Prem Narayan Rai,
learned counsel for the petitioners and Sri Anubhav Chandra, learned standing counsel for the State-respondents.

sentences.text: Learned standing counsel states on instructions that a Case Crime No.208 of 2021 under Sections 420, 414 I.P.C. was registered against some persons who were indulged in purchase and sale of stolen vehicles and accordingly investigation was carried but the respondents have not got closed shops of any of the petitioners.

He further states that the fact is that when investigation/ verification was being made,
the shopkeepers themselves fled away closing their shops so as to avoid verification.

Be that as it may, the petitioners may raise their grievances individually before the Commissioner of Police, Meerut, who shall look into the matter and take appropriate action in accordance with law within three weeks from the date of submission of a representation, along with a certified copy of this order.

The Commissioner of Police,
Meerut shall further ensure that none of the petitioners are unnecessarily harassed and action be taken against them only in accordance with law, if required.
It is made clear that if any investigation by police is going on, then the petitioners shall fully cooperate in investigation.
With the aforesaid directions, the writ petition is disposed of.

It is made clear that we have not expressed any opinion on merits of the case of the petitioners."
5.
The present contempt proceedings has been initiated against the opposite parties for not complying the order of the writ Court.

6. An affidavit on behalf of Senior Superintendent of Police, Meerut, opposite party No.1, was filed on 22.09.2023 wherein, in para 4, it has been stated that on 02.08.2021 a raid was conducted in the shops of old Auto Parts situated in Sotiganj on the allegation that sale and purchase of stolen vehicle and Motor Parts were being carried out in the market.

In the police raid, old Auto Parts of stolen vehicles from shop of Junaid, Arshad, Sajid @ Nepali and Riazwan @ Kochu were recovered and an FIR being Case Crime No.208 of 2021 under Sections 414, 420 IPC was registered at P.S. Sadar Bazar, Meerut.

In para 5, it has been averred that during course of investigation, the Investigating Officer issued notice under Section 91 Cr.P.C. to all the old Auto Parts sellers to produce the list of Auto Parts/goods available in their shops/godown and also produce the bills of their sale and purchase.
The reply to the said notice was to be submitted within five days and till then the goods were not to be removed.
The police further informed that those, who failed to furnish the required information/document, cannot continue sale and purchase of goods in their premises in violation of notice.

In para 6 it has been averred that post issuance of notice under Section 91Cr.P.C., all traders of stolen Auto Parts in the Sotiganj Market closed their shops and removed the goods from their shops/godown.
Few of the shopkeepers submitted their affidavits with regard to the fact that in future they will not be indulged in sale and purchase of stolen Auto Parts of vehicle.
Further none of the applicants have submitted required information to the police of Sadar Bazar, Meerut.

7. Further, in para 7 it has been averred that except the issuance of notice by the Investigating Officer under Section 91 Cr.P.C., no written or oral order was passed against the traders of old Auto M/S Sharma Old Body Parts And 19 Others vs Sri Rohit Singh Sajwan, Ssp/ Police ... on 15 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/23489882/
2
Parts in Sotiganj Market for closing of their shops, but, they have closed their shops and removed the goods which were kept there.
In para 8 it has been averred that after investigation, charge sheet has been submitted in Case Crime No.208 of 2021 against the accused persons.
In para 9, it has been averred that the earlier officer has been transferred and the deponent has taken charge.

He held a press conference in which he assured the Auto Parts Traders of Sotiganj Market that there was no restriction on running the business in the market, but, he also informed that they will not be permitted to indulge in sale and purchase of stolen vehicles and Auto Parts and if they were found involved in such activity, strict action will be taken against them.
In para 10 of the affidavit, it is categorically stated that no criminal case is lodged against the applicants in regard to stolen vehicles.

Further in paras 11 and 12 it has been mentioned that except the shops of few old Auto Parts seller in the Sotiganj Market, all other shops of electrical goods, electronics, readymade garments are open and the shopkeepers are doing their business peacefully.

In para 13, it has been stated that police of Sadar Bazar, Meerut has made a physical verification regarding the shop of applicant No.1 and found that he alongwith his brother are carrying on the business of Electrical and Electronic goods from their shop in question.

Similarly, applicant No.16 is running the Crane business from his shop and applicant No.18 is running business of battery repairing from his shop,
while the shop of the applicant No.6 is situated in the building of one Rahul Kala alias Imran and the building is seized by the District Magistrate, Meerut under Section 14(1) of The Uttar Pradesh Gangsters and Anti-Social Activities (Prevention) Act.

sentences.text: 8. A counter affidavit has been filed by the applicant to the affidavit filed by the opposite party No.1 wherein the said paragraphs have been denied.
In para 5 it has been submitted that a notarized affidavit has been given by the applicants to the authorities.
In para 7 it has been stated that they are not in the business of stolen vehicles and Auto Parts.

9. Learned counsel for the applicants submitted that the police authorities are not permitting the applicants to run their business of old Auto Parts from their shops and whenever they open the shop, they are asked to closed down the same.
10. Learned Standing Counsel has denied the allegation made from the applicants' side and has reiterated the stand taken in the affidavit filed by the Superintendent of Police, Meerut.
11. I have heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the material on record.

12. From the reading of order dated 15.02.2023 passed in Writ C No.34843 of 2022, it is clear that after the instructions were placed before the writ Court, the writ Court had only permitted the petitioners/applicants to raise their grievance before the Commissioner of Police, Meerut who was to look into the matter and take appropriate action.
13. It is not disputed by both the parties that a raid was conducted on the business premises of certain old Auto Parts seller situated in Sotiganj Market, Meerut on 02.08.2021.
The police team had recovered old Auto Parts of stolen vehicles and a first information report was lodged against certain persons.

The police, in order to safeguard that no such illegal activity of selling stolen vehicle and old Auto Parts is carried out in the Sotiganj Market, it required all the old Auto Parts sellers to M/S Sharma Old Body Parts And 19 Others vs Sri Rohit Singh Sajwan, Ssp/ Police ... on 15 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/23489882/
3 produce the list of Auto Parts and the goods in their shops/godowns.
There was no written order by the police authorities to close down their shops or to discontinue their business.
The sole requirement was to furnish documents which tallied with the goods which were sold from these Auto Part shops.

14. Those old Auto Parts sellers, who where carrying out illegal business without any documents,
preferred not to carry on the business and closed down their establishment.

From the affidavit filed by the opposite party No.1 it seems that the old Auto Parts were removed from their shops and godowns as they were afraid that during investigation they would fail to produce the documents and their goods would be seized and they would be prosecuted for selling the Auto Parts of stolen vehicles as was the case in Case Crime No.208 of 2021.

15. There is no denial to the fact that the applicant No.1 is carrying on the business of Electrical and Electronic goods from their shop and similarly other applicants are also carrying on different business.
In the counter affidavit filed by them, they have not denied the averments made in the affidavit filed by the Senior Superintendent of Police, Meerut.

16. Thus, it is clear that the writ Court had only provided an opportunity to the applicants to raise their grievance before the authorities who was to be look into the matter and take appropriate action.

The police authorities had given sufficient opportunity to the Auto Parts sellers to come up with documents showing that they were not indulging in sale of Auto Parts of stolen vehicles and the business, which is being carried out, is in fair and transparent manner.
17. Considering the facts and circumstances of the case, I find that no case for contempt is made out against the opposite parties.

Moreover, the district administration as well as the police authorities have acted in a fair manner and had only stopped the illegal business of Auto Parts of stolen vehicles which was being carried out in Sotiganj Market of Meerut for a long time.

The effort of the police department needs appreciation as they have dealt with the matter with utmost integrity and honesty and had not harassed any trader or businessman who is in genuine business of Auto Parts.
It is only those traders and businessman who were engaged in the illegal business of Auto Parts of stolen vehicles, are in fear as their business would come to an end.
18. This Court finds that no indulgence can be given while exercising jurisdiction under Section 12 of the Contempt of Courts Act.
19. The contempt application is misconceived and stands dismissed.
Order Date :- 15.5.2024
